I’ve been steadily losing weight. People at work comment that I look thinner, and my clothes are looser. Part of me notices that and thinks I should probably stop, but I keep tightening the rules anyway. I avoid things like pizza, burgers, anything I think is “heavy,” because I’m worried that if I eat them I’ll put on weight really fast, like it’ll show up the next day.

At the same time, my mood’s been off. I feel kind of flat and tired a lot, like I’m just going through the motions—work, home, sleep. I don’t really feel like hanging out with friends anymore, and even stuff I used to enjoy just feels sort of pointless.

I’ve cut my intake down to the bare minimum—mostly black coffee, water, and maybe a small salad or some plain vegetables once a day. I check calorie counts obsessively. If something feels “too much,” like bread, pasta, or anything fried or sugary, I just won’t touch it. I feel like if I eat those, I’ll blow up overnight.

I weigh myself multiple times a day, and the number has been steadily dropping. People at work keep saying I look “too thin,” but when I look in the mirror I still feel like there’s fat I need to get rid of. The idea of gaining even a couple of pounds really scares me.

At the same time, I’ve been feeling pretty low—no energy, not really interested in hanging out with friends, trouble enjoying the few things I used to like, like gaming on my nights off. But even when I’m down, the fear of putting on weight is always there and kind of overrules everything else.
D021-D013_h001.question_b:

My appetite’s basically gone. Some nights I’ll realize I’ve only had a sandwich all day, maybe some coffee. It’s not that I’m trying to cut calories or anything; I just don’t feel hungry and it feels like too much effort to eat. I have lost weight—my coworkers have commented on it—but it wasn’t on purpose. Honestly, I’m not really thinking about my weight at all.

I’m exhausted all the time, even if I sleep 10–12 hours after my shift. My concentration at work is shot; I’ll catch myself staring at server logs and not processing anything. D021-D013_h023.question_both:
I’ve been feeling off for maybe a couple of months now, it’s hard to pin down exactly. Working nights in the ER, I just… stopped really eating regular meals. I’ll grab a yogurt or a couple of bites of something and feel like that’s enough. If I sit down with a full plate, I get uncomfortable and push most of it around, maybe take a bite or two and then lose interest. Part of it is that I don’t like the idea of putting on any weight; even a small change on the scale makes me anxious, so it’s easier to just keep things “light.”

I’ve noticed my scrubs getting loose, my period’s been irregular, I get dizzy during long shifts, and my hair seems thinner when I put it up. But I just tell myself it’s stress, bad hospital coffee, and weird hours. Emotionally, I do feel more drained than usual, kind of flat and disconnected, like I’m on autopilot. On my days off I mostly stay in, don’t really feel like seeing friends or doing much. But I can still get through my shifts, so I keep telling myself it’s not that serious.
D021-D013_h023.question_a:
I guess this really started about six months ago. I’ve been cutting down what I eat more and more. On a typical day I might have a coffee before my shift and then just pick at half a granola bar or a few bites of salad during my break. Sometimes I just push food around and say I’m not hungry. I feel better when my stomach is empty; if I eat a “normal” portion I feel disgusting and guilty.

I’m terrified of putting on weight. Even a pound freaks me out. I check my body in the mirror all the time, pinch at my sides, and if my scrubs feel the slightest bit tighter I’ll skip dinner. People at work keep saying I look too thin, but when I look at myself I still see areas that need to be “leaner.”

Physically I’ve been lightheaded during long shifts, my hair is thinning, and I haven’t had my period for a few months, but I keep telling myself it’s just stress from nights in the ER. Lately I’ve also felt really down, exhausted, not enjoying much outside of work—like a low-grade depression—but even when I’m sad, the thing I obsess about most is not getting fat.
D021-D013_h023.question_b:
It’s been about four, maybe five months now that I’ve just felt…flat. I drag myself to the ER, do my twelve-hour shifts, but it’s like I’m on autopilot. When I get home, I just crawl into bed. I used to go out with coworkers after nights; now I ignore their texts. Even on my days off, I can’t make myself do anything except scroll on my phone and stare at the wall.

My appetite’s basically disappeared. Some shifts I realize I’ve only had a couple bites of whatever I packed. It’s not that I’m trying to lose weight or scared of getting fat—I honestly don’t care how I look right now—I just have no interest in food. My scrubs are looser, and people comment I look thinner, but it’s more like a side effect of not caring than a goal.

I wake up hours before my alarm with this heavy dread, replaying every mistake at work. I feel guilty, worthless, like I’m letting patients and my family down. I cry in the staff bathroom between patients, then wipe my face and keep going, feeling completely empty.
